analyses.title: Entry-point granularity: per-item open vs. bulk folder picker
analyses.description:
In the scenario of single or few-item manual uploads on Android, Google Photos' per-item "open photo/video then Back up now" pattern and Dropbox's "+ → Upload Photos → tap to select → Set location → Upload" pattern represent two distinct entry-point granularities. Based only on official help text, this comparison is bounded to documented behavior.
【推断】场景：Mobile manual photo upload: new Android user uploading a small batch from camera roll.

analyses.title: Common pattern: multi-select via long-press/tap-to-pick with explicit final action
analyses.description:
Across both Google Photos and Dropbox mobile, official help describes multi-item selection (Google Photos: touch and hold then tap Back up; Dropbox: tap the photos to upload then tap Set location/Upload). The pattern is "select items, then confirm an explicit final action," which is a shared mobile upload convention observed in two sampled products.
【推断】场景：Mobile manual photo upload where user wants to back up several items at once.

analyses.title: Consider a confirmation affordance before final upload tap
analyses.description:
Based on the documented Dropbox steps "tap the photos…Tap Set location…Tap Upload" and Google Photos "Tap Back up now," a recommendation worth human evaluation is to surface a brief confirmation (e.g., count of selected files or an undo window) at the final action. Recommendation only; no claim of measured effect on mis-tap rates.
【建议】场景：Mobile manual photo upload entry points where a user may have selected the wrong items.
